s: Welcome to Word Kitchen, the show where we cook up new English words together.
Let us start with the one we touch all day long.
Lena, how many hours a day do your fingers spend on a keyboard?
My laptop keyboard is my best friend and my worst enemy.
I learned to type fast because my keyboard broke at work and I had to use an old one.
An old keyboard with sticky keys?
I actually bought a wireless keyboard last year, and my hands are much happier.
A wireless keyboard is a game changer.
But tell me, Lena, what happens when the power runs out?
Then we talk about the battery.
My phone battery never survives a full day.
I check the battery percentage about fifty times a day.
If the battery drops below twenty percent, I start to panic.
Twenty percent is my danger zone too.
I always carry a power bank, but the real problem is the battery in my old tablet.
But you know what saves me every day?
I have three chargers, and I still lose all of them.
I bought a new charger for the office, another charger for home, and a tiny charger for my bag.
And the charger is always in the other room.
The real question is why we even need the charger so often.
I get a notification, then another notification, then ten more.
I turned off half my notifications last month, and I feel so much calmer.
A notification is not always important.
I missed a flight once because I ignored the notification from the airline app.
So maybe keep the travel notifications on.
Now, speaking of apps, let us talk about safety.
My password is strong, but I have to remember a different password for every account.
If you reuse the same password everywhere, one hack opens every door.
I use a password manager now.
It creates a random password for me, and I only remember one main password.
A good password should be long and strange, not your birthday.
I always press remind me later when my phone asks me to update.
Then I forget to update for weeks.
But you really should update your device regularly, because an update often fixes security problems.
Last month I finally ran the update, and my phone felt brand new.
So yes, update early, update often.
And while the update is running, what do we usually do?
We download apps, music, and movies.
I downloaded three new apps this morning.
My storage is full because I download every episode and never delete them.
At least you can download them and listen offline.
A slow internet connection makes every download painful, though.
Okay, next word, and this one is a lifesaver: backup.
I keep a backup of my photos in the cloud, and another backup on an external drive.
My laptop died, and I had no backup at all.
Now the backup runs automatically every night.
I set mine up after I lost my notes.
A good backup means you never cry over a broken phone.
And speaking of phones, let us talk about the word device.
A device is any small machine: a phone, a tablet, a laptop.
How many devices do you own, Maya?
My phone, my laptop, my tablet, my watch.
I have three devices, and each device needs charging, updating, and protecting.
Every device is a small pet.
That is a funny way to see it.
My favorite device is my e-reader.
One device, one job, no notifications.
I want one device with no notifications too.
Software is what makes the device smart.
Without software, a phone is just an expensive brick.
The software on my laptop is old, so everything runs slowly.
I need to update the software, but I am lazy.
There is good free software for almost everything now.
Photo software, music software, even software for learning English.
The software in that app remembers our vocabulary.
Let us review our ten words quickly.
How many devices do you own?
Before we finish, a quick quiz.
Lena, what do you call the thing you type on?
And the thing that stores power?
And the messages that pop up on the screen?
And what keeps your account safe?
I think our listeners know these words now.
That is our tech menu for today.
Use these ten words this week, and they will stick.
And we will be back tomorrow with a fresh batch.
